transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hello, Doctor. Thank you so much for fitting me in. I hope I'm not taking up time that someone else might need more, but... well, my family suggested I come speak with you. 

It's probably nothing major, really, just some... little habits I've gotten into lately. I've sort of gotten stuck doing these little routines. It's nothing too terrible, just things like washing my hands again after I handle my wrist brace, or going back to recheck the stove and the front door. And sometimes I have this habit where I silently count through my steps before I leave the house. 

I know it probably sounds a bit silly, and I know in my head that I've already done enough, but I just keep doing it. It's actually starting to make me a little late for things, which is quite embarrassing. Does that make sense? I just wanted to make sure I'm doing the right thing by coming in to ask you about it.
Do these routines or thoughts cause you a lot of anxiety or distress, especially when you try to resist doing them?

Well, um... distress might be a bit of a strong word. I certainly don't want to overstate things or make a fuss. But... yes, I suppose it does make me quite uncomfortable if I try to just ignore them. 

For instance, I’ll just be sitting quietly reading at home, or getting ready for my volunteer shift at the museum, and... well, this ugly little thought just keeps barging in. It'll tell me that I’ve left something unsafe, or touched something unclean, or that I might somehow put someone at risk. 

I mean, I know perfectly well it’s completely out of proportion—I have my degree, I'm a rational person, after all! But the thought just sort of sits there, nagging at me, and it's so much easier to just do the routine than to sit there feeling anxious about it. I hope I'm explaining that properly. Does that sound like the sort of thing you usually hear from people?
How much time do these routines take out of your day, and do they interfere with your normal activities or cause you significant distress?

Well, um... as for the time, I really try not to let it take up too much of my day. I mean, I’m still managing perfectly well on my own, keeping up with the house and everything. I certainly don't want to paint a picture that I'm falling apart, because I'm not.

But... I suppose, if I’m being completely honest—and I do want to make sure I'm giving you the right information—it has started to get in the way just a little bit. I hate to admit it, it’s quite embarrassing, really... but these routines have actually made me late to my docent shifts a few times. And... well, there were a couple of extra museum events recently that I just ended up skipping entirely. Just because... going through all the checking and the counting just to get out the front door felt like... well, like it was just too much to tackle. 

I feel dreadful about it, honestly, letting people down like that. I hope that doesn't make me sound terribly irresponsible. Is that the sort of thing you needed to know?
Can you tell me more about those intrusive thoughts? Are they something you find disturbing or against your values, and do they keep coming back even when you wish they wouldn’t?

Yes, exactly. I know I touched on it a moment ago, and I do apologize if I’m repeating myself... but they really do just keep coming back, even when I try my hardest to ignore them. I’ll just be sitting there, trying to read a book at home, or getting my things together for a museum shift, and... well, there it is again. That same ugly little thought just barges right in. 

It just insists that I’ve left something unsafe, or that I’ve touched something unclean, or... well, this is the part I find most upsetting, really... that I might somehow put someone else at risk if I don't go back and fix it. It is quite disturbing to me, to be perfectly honest, because I would never, ever want to cause harm to anyone. It goes entirely against my nature. 

And the frustrating thing is, I know perfectly well it’s completely out of proportion! I try so hard to just push the thought away because it feels so foolish for a man my age to be worrying about such unlikely things. But it just won't leave me be until I do my little checks. I hope that answers your question properly? I just really hope you don't think I'm completely losing my mind...

When you perform these routines, like checking the stove or counting your steps, is it mainly to prevent something bad from happening rather than because you find the act itself enjoyable or satisfying?

Oh, heavens no, it’s certainly not enjoyable. I mean, I really wish I didn't feel the need to do any of it. You're quite right, it's entirely just to... well, to keep those bad things from happening, or at least to quiet that awful feeling. 

Actually, what finally brought me in to see you is that I’ve gotten quite stuck doing these... well, these little routines. It sounds so silly for a grown man, but... for instance, I have this wrist brace, and I find myself having to wash my hands again and again after just handling it. And then there's the rechecking of the stove, and the front door... and I even do this rather embarrassing thing where I silently count through my steps before I can finally bring myself to leave the house. 

It’s just... they’re starting to make me late for things, as I mentioned before, even when I know perfectly well I’ve already done enough. I know the door is locked, and I know my hands are clean, but I just can't seem to stop myself from doing the routine anyway. I hope I’m not coming across as completely absurd. Does that make sense? Is that what you meant by your question?
